chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no soul except that God, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed for it its sustenance as permissible, coming to it in good health; and He has also presented to it the forbidden from another direction. So if it takes anything from the forbidden, He deducts it from the permissible that He had decreed for it; and with God, beyond these two, there is abundant grace.
And that is His word, Mighty and Majestic: 'And ask God from His grace.'

key_terms.حَرَام: haram — forbidden, unlawful; what God has prohibited
key_terms.حَلَال: halal — permissible, lawful; what God has allowed
key_terms.رِزْق: rizq — divinely apportioned sustenance/provision; in Islamic theology, this is pre-determined by God for each soul
key_terms.عَافِيَة: 'afiya — safety, health, wellbeing; the state in which halal sustenance arrives
key_terms.فَضْل: fadl — grace, bounty, excess favour; additional provision from God beyond the assigned sustenance
key_terms.قَاصَّ: qassa — to offset, deduct, compensate; the divine mechanism of accounting between halal and haram

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about halal and haram sustenance (rizq) in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) teaches that God has pre-ordained halal sustenance for every soul, delivered in safety and wellbeing. However, God also places forbidden (haram) means before each person as a test. If one indulges in haram earnings, God compensates by reducing the halal that was divinely assigned, while still holding in reserve additional grace. The Imam substantiates this with Quran 4:32, encouraging believers to seek God's lawful bounty directly rather than resorting to forbidden means.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is none from a soul except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Necessitated for it it’s Permissible sustenance, given to him during its good health, and Presented to it the Prohibited from another aspect. So if it were to take anything from the Prohibited, there would be a reduction in it if from the Permissible which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Necessitated for it; and in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> besides these two, there is abundance Grace,
and there are the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic: “And they are asking Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from His<sup>azwj</sup> Grace”’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibrahim ibn abu al-Balad from his father who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

There is not a single soul whose sustenance Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has not assigned of the lawful kind and in good health. He has disclosed the unlawful kind also but in another aspect. If the soul achieves a certain amount of the unlawful kind it is reduced from its lawful sustenance which He has assigned for him. Besides these two kinds of sustenance, there is a great deal of extra with Allah
as is mentioned in the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘You must ask Allah to grant you (sustenance) from the extra with Him. . . .’ ( 3 : 37 )”
